mainTopic: Explaining the ברייתא about מעשר שני that entered ירושלים and left, the walls 'capturing' produce, מעשר שני worth less than a פרוטה, and how the חומש is calculated
overview: The גמרא is trying to explain a ברייתא that says מעשר שני which entered ירושלים and then left may not be redeemed. It first rejects reading the case as טמא produce, because רבי אלעזר says טמא מעשר שני may be redeemed even inside ירושלים. Next it tries food bought with מעשר שני money, following רבי יהודה, who says such food is buried. That reading fails too, so the גמרא explains the case as טהור produce whose city walls fell. רבא says walls 'capture' produce only by rabbinic decree, which seems to cover only standing walls. The answer is that the רבנן made no distinction between standing walls and fallen ones. רב ששת then reads the ברייתא as one case: produce worth less than a פרוטה, where the walls fell, and he teaches that even such small produce is captured. A new ברייתא learns from 'ממעשרו' that מעשר שני worth less than a פרוטה cannot be redeemed. אמוראים argue whether this means the produce itself or its חומש, and a ברייתא's word 'דיו' leaves a קשיא on the view that it means the produce itself. Finally the גמרא asks whether the חומש is counted from within or from without, and רבינא begins a proof that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Impure second tithe can be redeemed even in Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge using רבי אלעזר's teaching: טמא מעשר שני may be redeemed even inside ירושלים, because the Torah allows redemption when one 'cannot eat it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: [Impure second tithe can be redeemed] even in Jerusalem, as it says: 'For you are unable to carry it.' And 'carrying' here means nothing other than eating, as it says: 'And he took portions from before him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge. If the ברייתא is talking about טמא produce, why would it say the produce can't be redeemed? רבי אלעזר says טמא מעשר שני can be redeemed even inside ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר reads 'שאתו' as 'eating it,' and he proves this from the word 'משאת' (food portions) in בראשית. So the Torah allows redemption whenever you cannot eat the מעשר שני, and טמא produce cannot be eaten. That means טמא produce could be redeemed even inside the city, so the ברייתא cannot be talking about טמא produce.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe: produce that must be eaten in ירושלים, or redeemed for money
Redeemed: the holiness is moved onto money

phrases.english: even in Jerusalem
phrases.notes: This finishes רבי אלעזר's line from just before: impure second tithe may be redeemed even inside ירושלים.

phrases.english: as it is stated: 'For you are unable to carry it'
and 'se'et' means nothing other than eating
as it is stated: 'And he took portions from before him'
phrases.notes: בראשית 43:34. The 'portions' there were food, so the root means eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge that began before this section, against reading the ברייתא as talking about טמא produce.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that the ברייתא is talking about טמא מעשר שני
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If טמא מעשר שני can be redeemed even inside ירושלים, then the ברייתא's ruling against redeeming it after it left makes no sense.

steps.title: The case is food bought with second-tithe money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a new case. The ברייתא is talking about food bought with מעשר שני money, which cannot simply be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is talking about food bought with second-tithe money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the idea of טמא produce. It suggests the ברייתא means food that was bought with מעשר שני money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food bought with מעשר שני money (לקוח) is a 'second-generation' holy item. It has stricter rules for redemption than the original produce. That could explain why the ברייתא says it is not redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: Food bought with second-tithe money; it takes on מעשר שני holiness
'Rather': drops the earlier idea and offers a new one

phrases.english: Rather, with regard to food acquired with second-tithe money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by moving the ברייתא to a different case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was talking about ordinary טמא מעשר שני produce.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is talking about food bought with מעשר שני money.

steps.title: A משנה says impure purchased food can be redeemed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects. A משנה rules that food bought with מעשר שני money that became טמא should be redeemed, so the problem comes back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Food bought with second-tithe money should also be redeemed! For we learned: Food bought with second-tithe money that became impure should be redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new answer. It quotes a משנה that says even food bought with מעשר שני money gets redeemed once it becomes טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new case does not solve the problem. According to the משנה, טמא purchased food can be redeemed just like טמא produce. So a ruling of 'not redeemed' still doesn't fit.

phrases.english: Food acquired with tithe money too, let him redeem it,
as we learned: Food acquired with second-tithe money
that became impure should be redeemed!

steps.triggerLanguage: לָקוּחַ בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר נָמֵי לִיפְרְקֵיהּ, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא is talking about food bought with מעשר שני money
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה rules that טמא purchased food is redeemed, so the ברייתא's ruling against redemption still makes no sense.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who says to bury it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. He holds that טמא purchased food is buried, not redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רבי יהודה, who says: it must be buried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא saves the purchased-food explanation. It says the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who disagrees with that משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, purchased food that becomes טמא cannot be redeemed at all. It must be buried. So the ברייתא's 'not redeemed' fits his view.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who argues on the משנה about טמא purchased food

phrases.english: In accordance with Rabbi Yehuda,
who says: It must be buried.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by connecting the ברייתא to a different תנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a particular opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא follows the ruling of the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who says such food is buried.

steps.title: According to רבי יהודה, leaving the city should not matter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects. If the ruling follows רבי יהודה, the ברייתא had no reason to mention that the food left ירושלים, because he says it is buried either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it follows רבי יהודה, why specifically say 'it left'? Even if it did not leave, the same is true!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the רבי יהודה answer. It asks why the ברייתא would mention 'left' if that detail makes no difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, טמא purchased food is never redeemed, inside or outside ירושלים. So the ברייתא's detail of 'entered and left' would be pointless. This pushes the גמרא to look for a case where leaving the city really matters.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Why specifically?' Asks why a detail was mentioned

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Yehuda,
why specifically 'it exited'?
Even if it did not exit, the same applies!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the ברייתא according to רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's detail that the food left ירושלים would be unnecessary, since רבי יהודה rules the same way even if it never left.

steps.title: Pure produce, and 'left' means the walls fell
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new explanation. The produce is טהור, and 'left' means the walls of ירושלים fell, so the produce counts as outside the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: really it is talking about pure produce. And what does 'it left' mean? That the walls fell.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier ideas. It explains that the ברייתא is about טהור produce, and 'left' does not mean the produce was carried out but that the city walls collapsed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, once טהור מעשר שני enters the walls of ירושלים, the walls 'capture' it and it can no longer be redeemed. The ברייתא's new point is that this stays true even after the walls fall. The produce still may not be redeemed, even though it is now as if it were outside.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Really / actually': goes back to an earlier possibility
Partitions: here, the walls of ירושלים

steps.confusionAlert: 'יצא' here does not mean someone carried the produce out of the city. It means the walls fell, so the produce counts as outside without moving.

phrases.english: Rather: actually it is about pure produce,
and what is 'it exited'? That the partitions fell.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by redefining both the produce and the word 'יצא'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case and the wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'יצא' means the produce was physically taken out of ירושלים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The produce is טהור, and 'יצא' means the walls fell. Even so, the produce stays captured and is not redeemed.

steps.title: רבא: walls capture only by rabbinic decree, and only when standing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this from רבא. Walls 'capturing' produce is only a rabbinic rule, and the רבנן made that decree only while the walls are standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבא said: A wall for eating is Torah law; walls for capturing are rabbinic. And when the רבנן decreed, it was when the walls exist. When the walls don't exist, the רבנן did not decree!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the fallen-walls answer using a rule from רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says that eating מעשר שני inside the walls is a Torah law. But the idea that walls 'capture' produce so it can't be redeemed is only rabbinic. If the רבנן made that decree only for standing walls, then once the walls fall the produce should not be captured, and it should be redeemable.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To capture': the walls lock the produce in so it can't be redeemed

phrases.english: But didn't Rava say:
a partition for eating is by Torah law,
phrases.notes: He means the walls mark where you may eat מעשר שני.

phrases.english: partitions for capturing are by rabbinic law.
And when the Sages decreed,
it was when the partitions exist.
When the partitions do not exist,
the Sages did not decree!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that produce stays captured after the walls fall
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Capturing is only a rabbinic decree tied to standing walls. With no walls, there is no decree, so the produce should be redeemable.

steps.title: The רבנן made no distinction about standing walls
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that once the רבנן made the decree, they applied it to every case, whether the walls are standing or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן did not distinguish between when the walls exist and when they don't.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא's challenge. It says the rabbinic decree covers fallen walls too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the principle of 'לא פלוג': the רבנן make one clear rule and do not split it into different cases. So produce captured by the walls stays captured even after they fall. That explains the ברייתא's ruling that it is not redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The רבנן did not distinguish': a rabbinic rule applies the same way in all cases

steps.whatToRemember: In this first approach, the ברייתא is explained as טהור מעשר שני whose walls fell. It still may not be redeemed, because the רבנן's decree that walls 'capture' produce applies whether or not the walls are standing (לא פלוג). רב ששת gives a different explanation starting in the next step.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: a rabbinic decree is often applied across the board, even where its original reason seems missing.

phrases.english: The Sages did not distinguish
between when the partitions exist
and when the partitions do not exist.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 and secures the explanation from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying the principle of לא פלוג
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree that walls capture produce applies only while the walls are standing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The decree applies in every case, so produce stays captured even after the walls fall.

steps.title: רב ששת: the ברייתא describes one single case
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the ברייתא teaches one combined case: מעשר שני worth less than a פרוטה that entered ירושלים and then left.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה said in the name of רב ששת: The ברייתא is teaching one case. It is מעשר שני worth less than a פרוטה that went into ירושלים and then came out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new way to explain the ברייתא. רב ששת says all its details fit together as one single case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא had trouble explaining the ברייתא. רב ששת joins two details together: the food is worth less than a פרוטה, and it entered ירושלים and left. Together they explain why it cannot be redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money
Worth a פרוטה, the smallest coin that counts

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda said in the name of Rav Sheshet:
It is teaching one case:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה
phrases.english: second tithe that is not worth a peruta
that entered Jerusalem and went out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new explanation of the ברייתא instead of the earlier ones.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the ברייתא as one combined case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's details seemed hard to explain together.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is talking about one case: מעשר שני worth less than a פרוטה that entered ירושלים and left.

steps.title: Why not bring it back in and eat it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the owner doesn't just bring the produce back into ירושלים and eat it there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why can't he do anything with it? Let him bring it back into ירושלים and eat it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת's case. If the food left ירושלים, the owner could simply carry it back in and eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not being able to redeem the food is not a real problem if it can still be eaten in ירושלים. So why does the ברייתא treat it as a problem case?

keyTerms.meaning: And let him bring it in

phrases.english: Why?
Let him go back, bring it in, and eat it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the case described in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's case of produce that left ירושלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Food that left ירושלים can be brought back in and eaten, so there is no problem.

steps.title: The walls fell
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the walls of ירושלים fell, so the food cannot be eaten there.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where the walls fell.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the walls of ירושלים had fallen, so bringing the food back in doesn't help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating מעשר שני needs the walls of ירושלים to be standing. With the walls down, the owner cannot eat it there, so the question of redeeming it comes back.

phrases.english: Where the walls fell.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He could just eat it in ירושלים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The walls fell, so it cannot be eaten there.

steps.title: Then let him redeem it, based on רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the walls fell, he should be allowed to redeem it, since according to רבא the walls 'capture' produce only by rabbinic law and only while standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him redeem it! Didn't רבא say: walls that allow eating are from the Torah, walls that capture are only rabbinic. And the רבנן made their decree only when the walls are standing. When the walls are not standing, the רבנן did not decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again, using רבא's rule. This is the same challenge as Step 7, now aimed at רב ששת's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא splits the walls' power in two. Allowing eating comes from the Torah, but 'capturing' (blocking redemption) is only a rabbinic decree. If that decree is only for standing walls, fallen walls should not block redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: The wall's power to allow eating
The wall's power to capture, so the produce can no longer be redeemed

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two powers of the walls. 'Eating' is from the Torah and needs standing walls, but 'capturing' is only a rabbinic decree.

phrases.english: And let him redeem it?
But didn't Rava say:
the wall for eating is Torah law,
the wall for capturing is rabbinic,
phrases.notes: 'Capturing' means once the produce entered the walls, it is stuck as ירושלים produce and can't be redeemed.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי גְּזַרוּ רַבָּנַן – כִּי אִיתַנְהוּ לִמְחִיצוֹת.
phrases.english: and when the Rabbis decreed, it was when the walls are standing.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לֵיתַנְהוּ לִמְחִיצוֹת – לָא גְּזַרוּ רַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: When the walls are not standing, the Rabbis did not decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 11 using רבא, repeating the challenge of Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that fallen walls stop the produce from being redeemed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Capturing is only rabbinic and only for standing walls, so with fallen walls redemption should be allowed.

steps.title: The רבנן did not make a distinction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the רבנן applied their decree in all cases, whether the walls stand or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן did not make a difference between the cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as Step 8. Once the רבנן made the decree, it applies even after the walls fall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer limits רבא's statement. The decree may have started because of standing walls, but the רבנן made it one rule for everything. So the produce stays captured and cannot be redeemed.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן did not distinguish between cases

phrases.english: The Rabbis did not distinguish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12, as in Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The rabbinic decree is applied the same way everywhere
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree is only for standing walls.
steps.terutzMaskana: The decree applies even when the walls have fallen.

steps.title: Why mention less than a פרוטה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if fallen walls still capture, why does the ברייתא mention produce worth less than a פרוטה? The same would be true for more.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it mention specifically produce not worth a פרוטה? Even if it is worth a פרוטה, it would be the same!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions the wording of the ברייתא. If the walls capture any produce, the detail 'less than a פרוטה' seems unneeded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After Step 13, what blocks redemption is the walls, not the low value. So why did the ברייתא add a detail that doesn't seem to matter?

phrases.english: If so,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אִירְיָא אֵין בּוֹ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה?
phrases.english: why specifically produce not worth a peruta?
Even if it is worth one, the same would be true!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מַאי אִירְיָא אֵין בּוֹ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer of Step 13 to question the ברייתא's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's detail 'not worth a פרוטה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the walls capture all produce, the low value adds nothing.

steps.title: Teaching even the less obvious case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא teaches the bigger חידוש: even produce worth less than a פרוטה is captured by the walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is saying 'it's not even needed.' It's not needed to say that produce worth a פרוטה is captured by the walls. But produce worth less than a פרוטה, I might have said the walls don't capture it. So it teaches us that they do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא picked the harder case on purpose. Produce worth a פרוטה is obviously captured, so it teaches that even less than a פרוטה is captured.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the 'לא מיבעיא' style: teach the less obvious case, and the obvious case is understood. One might think something so small is not important enough to be captured by the walls. The ברייתא tells us it is.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not even necessary to say

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב ששת, the walls of ירושלים capture מעשר שני even after they fall, and even when it is worth less than a פרוטה.

phrases.english: He is speaking in the style of 'it is not necessary.'
It is not necessary to say when it is worth a peruta
that the walls capture it.
But when it is not worth a peruta,
I might say: the walls do not capture it,
so it teaches us that they do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: 'Not necessary' style: teaching the less obvious case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The detail 'less than a פרוטה' is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that even such small produce is captured by the walls.

steps.title: A פסוק excludes מעשר שני worth less than a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from 'ממעשרו', 'of his tithe', that מעשר שני worth less than a פרוטה cannot be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'If a man will redeem of his tithe.' 'Of his tithe' means not all of his tithe. This leaves out מעשר שני worth less than a פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא. It shows where we learn that מעשר שני worth less than a פרוטה cannot be redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ממעשרו', 'of his tithe', suggests only some of his tithe can be redeemed. The ברייתא says the part left out is מעשר שני worth less than a פרוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Of his tithe, meaning only part of it

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"If a man will surely redeem of his tithe"
"Of his tithe" means not all of his tithe.

phrases.aramaic: פְּרָט לְמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה.
phrases.english: This excludes second tithe that is not worth a peruta.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אִם גָּאֹל יִגְאַל אִישׁ מִמַּעַשְׂרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic, giving the source for the rule that less than a פרוטה cannot be redeemed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעשר שני worth less than a פרוטה cannot be redeemed, learned from 'ממעשרו'.

steps.title: Less than a פרוטה: the produce or its fifth?
steps.stepSummary: אמוראים argue what must be less than a פרוטה: the produce itself, or the extra fifth (חומש) paid when redeeming.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: רב אמי says: when the produce is not worth a פרוטה. רב אסי says: when its fifth is not worth a פרוטה. רבי יוחנן says: when the produce is not worth a פרוטה. רבי שמעון בן לקיש says: when its fifth is not worth a פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an argument about how to read the ברייתא. Two pairs of אמוראים argue the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side says the produce itself must be worth less than a פרוטה to be left out. The other side says it is enough that the added fifth is worth less than a פרוטה. That means a larger amount of produce would also be left out.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introducing an argument of אמוראים)
Its fifth: the extra amount added when redeeming

steps.confusionAlert: 'אין בו' and 'אין בחומשו' sound alike but are very different. One is about the produce's own value, and the other is about the extra fifth, which is much smaller.

phrases.english: It was stated:
Rav Ami says: when it is not worth a peruta.
Rav Asi says: when its fifth is not worth a peruta.
phrases.notes: The 'fifth' is the extra payment a person adds when he redeems his own מעשר שני.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: when it is not worth a peruta.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: אֵין בְּחוּמְשׁוֹ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says: when its fifth is not worth a peruta.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר. רַב אַמֵּי אָמַר: אֵין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the meaning of 'not worth a פרוטה' in the ברייתא of Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is an argument whether the produce or its fifth must be worth less than a פרוטה.

steps.title: A ברייתא about tiny מעשר שני is brought as a challenge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: for מעשר שני worth less than a פרוטה, it is enough to say that it and its חומש are transferred onto coins already used for redemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: מעשר שני that is not worth a פרוטה: it is enough for him to say, 'It and its extra fifth are made חולין onto the first coins.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge one of the opinions from Step 17. This step only quotes the source; the next step explains exactly whom it challenges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives a simple fix for tiny מעשר שני. Instead of a new redemption, the owner attaches it to coins that already carry the קדושה of מעשר שני from an earlier redemption. The key word to watch is 'דיו', 'it is enough'. The challenge in the next step is built on that word.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a תנאי source)
Made חולין (non-holy) by transferring the holiness
The first coins, already used to redeem מעשר שני earlier

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה –
phrases.english: Second tithe that does not have the value of a peruta –
it is enough that he says
"It and its fifth are made non-holy
onto the first coins."
phrases.notes: These are coins he already used to redeem other מעשר שני, so they are already holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to test the two opinions of Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that it is the produce itself that is worth less than a פרוטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Set up here; the word 'דיו' will be shown to fit only the other opinion (spelled out in Step 19).

steps.title: The word 'enough' fits only one opinion
steps.stepSummary: 'דיו' makes sense if the produce is worth a פרוטה and only the חומש is not. If the produce itself is under a פרוטה, 'enough' makes no sense. The difficulty stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works for the one who says 'the fifth is not worth a פרוטה': that is why it says 'enough'. Even though the produce itself is worth a פרוטה, since the fifth is not, this transfer is fine. But for the one who says 'the produce is not worth a פרוטה', what does 'enough' mean? It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the challenge. The ברייתא's word 'enough' fits one opinion and does not fit the other, and the גמרא leaves it as an unanswered difficulty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Enough' suggests there was something real to redeem, so a simpler method is good enough. That fits if the produce is worth a פרוטה and only the small חומש is the problem. If the produce itself is worth less than a פרוטה, there is nothing that could be redeemed at all, so calling the transfer 'enough' sounds wrong. The גמרא ends with 'קשיא', a real difficulty that is not resolved.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's 'דיו' supports the view that the problem is a חומש worth less than a פרוטה. The other view remains with an unanswered קשיא.
steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' here is not a full rejection. It means the question stands without an answer, which is weaker than 'תיובתא'.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says "its fifth is not worth" –
that is why it teaches "it is enough,"

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דִּבְדִידֵיהּ אִית בֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: because even though the produce itself has the value,
since its fifth does not have it – it is fine.
But according to the one who says "it itself is not worth,"
what is "it is enough"? It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא from Step 18 attacks one opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that the produce itself is worth less than a פרוטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Enough' implies there was real value to redeem. That fails if the produce itself is under a פרוטה.

steps.title: Is the חומש counted from inside or outside?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: is the חומש one-fifth of the item's value, or one-fifth of the final total (a quarter of the value)?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: is the fifth from within, or is the fifth from without?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the חומש was just discussed, the גמרא opens a new question about how to calculate it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'From within' means a fifth of the item's value: an item worth 20 needs 4 extra. 'From without' means a fifth of the final payment, which equals a quarter of the value: an item worth 20 needs 5 extra, for a total of 25. The question is how big the extra payment really is.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the Sages
The fifth from within: a fifth of the item's value
The fifth from without: a fifth of the total, a quarter of the value

steps.confusionAlert: 'From without' does not mean a bigger fraction of the total. It is still a fifth, but a fifth of the final sum, so it comes out to a quarter of the original value.

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
Is the fifth from within, or is the fifth from without?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the פרוטה discussion and starts a new question about the חומש.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the חומש is a fifth of the item's value or a fifth of the total payment.

steps.title: רבינא begins a proof from owners redeeming הקדש
steps.stepSummary: רבינא quotes a משנה (in ערכין): if the owner and another person both offer 20, the owner comes first because he adds a חומש. The משנה then begins the case of someone else offering 21, and it continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Come and hear: if the owners say 20 and anyone else says 20, the owners come first because they add a fifth. If one person said, 'I will pay 21'...
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא starts bringing a proof to answer the question. The משנה is only partly quoted here. Its ending, which holds the proof, comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner is preferred because his חומש makes his real payment larger than a stranger's 20. The משנה then compares offers of 21 and more. How big the owner's payment counts as being will show which way the חומש is calculated. The proof is not finished yet.

phrases.english: Ravina said: Come and hear:
If the owners say: for twenty,
phrases.notes: He means 20 dinars to redeem property given to the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: and any other person says: for twenty –
the owners come first, because they add a fifth.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אֶחָד: הֲרֵי עָלַי בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְאֶחָד –
phrases.english: If one person said: It is upon me for twenty-one –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of Step 20 with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: How the חומש is calculated (from within or from without)
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about owners and other people bidding to redeem הקדש
